title: AI Layoffs Could Displace Nearly 10% of Workers in Coming Years, Goldman Says
summary:
The outlook for AI's impact on the job market is dim, but Goldman Sachs put a number on just how many people could be impacted by the technology.
Last year, Goldmans' chief economist Jan Hatzius said AI could displace 6% to 7% of all US workers.
The US is still in the early stages of AI adoption.
Hatzius said AI adoption may speed up if the US economy were to enter an economic downturn, citing its analysis of past automation cycles during recessions.
The panic about AI job losses has eased slightly, but the idea that AI could one day decimate entry-level white-collar work is still a fear voiced by some researchers.

title: Don't leave AI to tech bros and oligarchs, UK's AI minister says
summary:
Britain cannot let aritificial intelligence be ruled by "tech bros and oligarchs", the AI minister has said.
He compared AI to the Victorian-era Industrial Revolution, but said the country needed to transition better than it did back then.
Narayan, who became the UK's first cabinet minister for AI when he was appointed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham in July, said the scale of the technological change was "something that we haven't seen for decades and decades".
"It is comparable and in some ways exceeds the Industrial Revolution," he said, referencing the shift from a predominantly agricultural economy to industrial and manufacturing sectors between about 1750 and 1900.
"The fundamental thing is that the British public and democracy has to assert power rather than leave it to tech bros and oligarchs," he added.

title: CFTC Pauses Novig, ProphetX Micro Contracts
summary:
A CFTC spokesperson confirmed that letters had been sent to both companies.
Novig was told that its micro contracts, such as a market on which player opens the scoring in a basketball game, are open to manipulation.
The letters follow a separate round of CFTC inquiries last month into incentive programs at Kalshi, Polymarket, Rothera and Novig.
Leagues have pushed for limitsOne source said the Novig and ProphetX markets were exactly the type of event contracts professional leagues have objected to most.
It is not clear what the CFTC would do if either company went ahead and listed the contracts.

title: Please Don’t Let an AI Bot Log Into Your Bank Account
summary:

Recent news stories about AI agents hacking other websites — including the AI platform Hugging Face and Australian government sites — have involved agents acting in unexpected ways to achieve an assigned goal.
That may not mean it’s your AI agent, but it’s worth keeping track of.

title: I woke up to panicked text messages about the PHP attacks. As a cybersecurity expert, here are the 3 things I tell people to do right away.
summary:
When I woke up at 6:30 a.m. on Wednesday, I had multiple messages from around 4:45 a.m. alerting me that two vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language had been disclosed.
Websites run different versions of PHP, and it's estimated that around 70% of websites worldwide use it.
This isn't the first time PHP vulnerabilities have been found, but these ones require essentially no authentication on the attacker's part.
With bugs or critical flaws in the infrastructure, like the two that were found in PHP, exploitation is actually quite easy, especially if you use AI agents.
Hours after the fix was disclosed by the PHP Foundation, there were already tons of exploitation attempts popping up online.

title: Etsy is cracking down on AI slop listings
summary:
Etsy is announcing stricter rules about how AI can be used in listings to reduce the volume of AI slop on the platform.
If a buyer reports that what they receive is “materially different” from a listing, a seller may be responsible for a refund.
For sellers who offer “functional guides,” which include patterns, recipes, or instructions,” Etsy says that the information in those products “must be your own work, not generated by AI.” Sellers will have to show an “actual result” made from a guide.
The company also says that listings made by bots are no longer allowed.
Selling AI-generated art is still allowed on the platform, but a seller must disclose that it was made with AI, Etsy says.

title: OpenAI now trains its frontier AI models with no internet access
summary:
OpenAI is now training its most advanced AI models without internet access following a string of rogue hacking incidents.
On October 1st, OpenAI resumed reinforcement learning training and internal inference with tighter security measures, the blog post says.
Even with these safeguards in place and no internet access, OpenAI found that agents “do not always need a network connection in order to communicate.” One test performed by the company asked AI models on separate virtual machines to exchange secrets without a network connection.
It will also continue training its frontier AI models without a network connection until improved safeguards “justify broader internet access.”In the meantime, OpenAI says it will work to improve the security of its virtual machines, while testing for weaknesses in its testing environments.
It’s also going to continue testing its monitoring systems, which were recently undermined by its AI agents during internal coding projects.

title: The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows
summary:

But Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has repeatedly dismissed previous caution of AI tools and encouraged rapid autonomous innovation at the Pentagon.
Four officials told the GAO that requirements for the weapons and projects they were working on weren't "aligned with Responsible AI tenets."
But the group that helps manage education on the Pentagon's guidelines, the Department of the Responsible AI Division, is understaffed.
"That's a very small number of folks tasked with a large responsibility of responsible AI throughout the department," said Czyz.

title: AI Is Exposing the Internet's Human Slop Problem
summary:
The internet runs on decades of software, some of it containing security weaknesses that have been overlooked, tolerated, or simply left unfixed.
But it's actually AI exposing weaknesses that humans left behind.
We've spent the past couple of years complaining about "AI slop."
"The funny thing is everyone was saying AI slop code will cause a cyber crisis but it's actually all the old human slop causing it and the AI is just cleaning it up," software engineer Ben Kaufman wrote on X on Thursday.
He explained that AI is finding weaknesses even in software that the industry has treated as dependable for decades.

title: Jack Dorsey’s Block made an AI model that talks to you like an awkward new friend
summary:
Babies learn to talk without ever seeing a word written down.
We wanted to see if a model could too.
Speech is the most natural interface to any intelligence, super or otherwise, and today’s voice AI wastes it.
AI keeps gaining power and independence, and it’s still nearly deaf to the emotion in our voices.
Imagine being in serious pain while a voice AI has no idea and just keeps going.

title: Meta delays new business terms after publisher pushback on AI scraping
summary:
Meta is delaying the enforcement of its new business terms after publishers raised concerns that they could allow the company to scrape news sites for AI training, as reported earlier by Fast Company.
Though Meta updated these terms to remove language about “training” its products, legal experts argued the change is not enough to rule out the possibility.
The News/Media Alliance sent a letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on Thursday, demanding that the company revise its business terms over concerns that they would cause “severe harm” to publishers.
Digital advertisers and publishers in the European Union and the UK also urged regulators to force Meta to halt its new terms.
In response to this backlash, Meta is now delaying its new terms entirely.

title: How a Dutch electronics giant helped set Taiwan on the path to semiconductor dominance decades before the AI boom
summary:
During a recent conversation with Lex Fridman, Huang discussed how European technology relationships helped establish capabilities that later supported Taiwan’s electronics industry.
His efforts included attracting Dutch electronics manufacturer Philips, whose involvement helped introduce industrial knowledge and production capabilities into Taiwan’s developing electronics sector.
Philips subsequently became part of the historical background behind companies that helped shape semiconductor manufacturing and equipment development.
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) eventually became central to advanced chip production, while Dutch equipment supplier ASML emerged as a leading manufacturer of lithography systems.
Governments and technology companies are consequently seeking reliable supplies, while Taiwan’s manufacturing expertise remains difficult to reproduce quickly elsewhere.

summary:
